mainTopic: One witness and silence: אביי's cases, and the מחלוקת between אביי and רבא about one witness to a wife's adultery
overview: The amud opens by finishing אביי's rule: when one witness accuses someone and that person stays silent, the witness is believed. The last of his three cases is an ox used for bestiality. A משנה in בכורות supports him, because it lists 'one witness' separately from 'the owner,' which only makes sense if the owner was silent. The גמרא then shows why אביי needed all three cases (חלב, טהרות, and the ox), since each has a different reason someone might stay quiet. Next comes a new question: is one witness believed when he says a man's wife was unfaithful and the husband is silent? אביי says yes. רבא says no, because a דבר שבערוה needs two witnesses. אביי brings two proofs: the story of the blind man and מר שמואל, and a long ברייתא about ינאי המלך, where a rumor that his mother was a captive was investigated and not found. רבא turns aside both proofs, explaining the ינאי story as two against two through הזמה or through רבי יצחק's swapped maidservant. The amud ends as רבא begins a new statement, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Third case: your ox was used for bestiality
steps.stepSummary: אביי's third case: a single witness says the owner's ox was used for bestiality, the owner stays silent, and the witness is believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one witness says, 'Your ox was used for bestiality,' and the owner says nothing, the witness is believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes אביי's list of cases where silence counts as admitting. This third case is about an ox becoming unfit as a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal used for bestiality cannot be brought on the מזבח. One witness alone is normally not enough to establish this. But because the owner does not deny it, the witness is believed, and the ox can no longer be used as a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: was used for bestiality (an animal that had relations with a person)

phrases.english: “Your ox was used for bestiality”
and the other one is silent — he is believed.

steps.triggerLanguage: שׁוֹרְךָ נִרְבַּע וְהַלָּה שׁוֹתֵק נֶאֱמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues אביי's list of cases from before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When one witness says an ox was used for bestiality and the owner stays silent, the witness is believed.

steps.title: Support from a משנה about an animal used for a sin
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה in בכורות: an animal used for a sin, or one that killed a person, is established by one witness or by the owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our תנא also taught this: if an animal was used for a sin, or it killed someone, and this is known through one witness or through the owner, he is believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a משנה that seems to back up אביי's ox case. The next step will show exactly how it backs him up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says one witness is enough to make such an animal unfit. That sounds surprising, because usually one witness cannot establish such a fact. The גמרא will now show that this must be talking about a case where the owner was silent.

keyTerms.meaning: our תנא (the author of a משנה) also taught this
a sin was done with it

phrases.english: And the תנא of our משנה also taught this:
and an animal with which a sin was done,
or that killed a person,
on the word of one witness
or on the word of the owner — he is believed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנָּא תּוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source that seems to support step 1.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's ruling that one witness is believed about an ox used for bestiality when the owner is silent.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in בכורות: an animal used for a sin becomes unfit 'על פי עד אחד'.

steps.title: Showing the משנה must mean the owner was silent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'one witness' means in the משנה. If the owner admitted, that is already the case of 'the owner,' so it must mean the owner stayed silent.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case is 'by one witness'? If the owner admits, that is the same as 'by the owner.' So doesn't it have to be where the owner stays silent?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that the משנה's 'one witness' case must be a case where the owner was quiet, exactly like אביי said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists two separate cases: 'one witness' and 'the owner.' If 'one witness' meant the owner agreed, it would just repeat the second case. So it must mean the owner said nothing, and the witness is still believed. That matches אביי.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the case? / what are the circumstances?

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה in בכורות counts 'one witness' separately from 'the owner,' which shows that silence works like an admission. This supports אביי.

phrases.aramaic: הַאי ״עַל פִּי עֵד אֶחָד״, הֵיכִי דָמֵי?
phrases.english: This case of “on the word of one witness” — what are its circumstances?
If the owner admits it,
that is the same as “on the word of the owner”!
Rather, is it not where he stays silent?

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי עַל פִּי עֵד אֶחָד הֵיכִי דָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the proof by showing how the משנה supports אביי.
steps.raayaObject: Silence of the owner counts as admission.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה lists 'one witness' and 'the owner' as separate cases.

steps.title: Why the חלב case alone is not enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why אביי needed more than the first case. In the חלב case, silence clearly means he agrees, because he brings a קרבן. In the טהרות case, he might be silent only because he doesn't care much.
steps.simpleTranslation: All the cases are needed. If he had taught only the first case (חלב), I would say the reason is: if he weren't sure he sinned, he would never bring a non-holy animal into the עזרה. But with 'your pure foods became impure,' I would say he is quiet because he thinks the food is still fine for him on days when he is impure anyway.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an unspoken question: why did אביי need several cases? It starts by showing that the חלב case cannot teach us the טהרות case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the חלב case, the man brings a קרבן. If he were not truly sure he sinned, that would mean bringing חולין into the עזרה, which is forbidden. So his silence surely means he agrees. In the טהרות case, nothing like that happens, and he may simply not bother to argue because he loses very little.

keyTerms.meaning: and it is necessary (all the cases are needed)
non-holy animals in the Temple courtyard (forbidden)

steps.confusionAlert: 'הָךְ קַמַּיְיתָא' (the first case) is the חלב case from before this section. It is not the ox case in step 1.

phrases.english: And it is necessary to teach all the cases,
for if he had taught us only that first case,
phrases.notes: The first case is 'you ate חלב,' where the man would have to bring a קרבן חטאת.

phrases.aramaic: אִי לָאו דְּקִים לֵיהּ בְּנַפְשֵׁיהּ דַּעֲבַד –
phrases.english: if he were not sure in himself that he did it,
he would not bring a non-sacred animal into the Temple courtyard.
But with “your pure foods became impure” —
we would say:
the reason he is silent is because he thinks,
it is fit for him in his days of impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּצְרִיכָא דְּאִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן הָךְ קַמַּיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the proof and turns to why אביי listed several cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: showing that each case has its own reason
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without the טהרות case, one might think silence counts only where the person acts on it, as in the חלב case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The טהרות case teaches that silence counts even where the person might be quiet because he loses little.

steps.title: Why the טהרות case alone is not enough: the ox case is needed too
steps.stepSummary: If אביי had taught only the טהרות case, one might say silence counts there only because he loses his pure food on pure days. With the ox, the owner might be quiet because not every ox is meant for the מזבח anyway. So all the cases are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he had taught us only this case (טהרות), I would say it is because he causes him a loss on his pure days. But with 'his ox was used for bestiality,' the owner would say: 'Not all oxen are meant for the מזבח.' So it is necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining why each case is needed. It shows that the ox case adds something the טהרות case cannot teach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the טהרות case there is a real loss, since he can't eat the food on days when he is pure. So his silence looks like agreement. In the ox case the owner loses very little, since not every ox is meant for the מזבח anyway. So we might think his silence means nothing, and אביי had to teach that even here the witness is believed.
steps.whatToRemember: Each of אביי's three cases teaches something new. חלב: silence plus bringing a קרבן. טהרות: silence even when the person might not care much. Ox: silence even when the loss seems tiny. In all three, the one witness is believed.

phrases.english: And if he had taught us only this case,

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּקָא מַפְסֵיד לֵיהּ בִּימֵי טׇהֳרָתוֹ,
phrases.english: it is because he causes him a loss in his days of purity,
but with “his ox was used for bestiality”
he would say:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל השְׁווֹרִים לָאו לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ קָיְימִי,
phrases.english: Not all oxen are standing ready for the altar,
phrases.notes: He means: losing the chance to offer this ox is no big deal to him, so he doesn't bother denying it.

phrases.english: so it is necessary.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן הָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the צריכותא that began in step 4.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All three of אביי's cases are needed, because each one has a different possible reason for staying silent, and in every case the witness is believed.

steps.title: What if one witness says the wife was unfaithful and the husband is silent?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the rule of 'one witness plus silence' also works when the witness says a man's wife committed adultery.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: If one witness says a man's wife was unfaithful, and the husband stays silent, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question. It takes the pattern from אביי's earlier cases (one witness, owner stays silent) and applies it to a wife who is accused of adultery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier cases (חלב, טהרות, the ox), silence was treated as agreeing with the witness. The new question is whether that works for a wife too, where the result would be very serious: she becomes forbidden to her husband.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked before them (the חכמים).
He stays silent; he does not deny it.

phrases.english: A question was asked before them:
His wife committed adultery, according to one witness,
and the husband is silent. What is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the 'one witness plus silence' rule from אביי's cases and asks whether it also applies to a wife accused of adultery.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the husband's silence make a single witness believed about his wife's adultery?

steps.title: אביי says he is believed; רבא says he is not
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the single witness is believed. רבא disagrees, because anything involving ערוה needs two witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: He is believed. רבא said: He is not believed, because this is a matter of forbidden relations, and such a matter needs at least two witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question in opposite ways. רבא also gives his reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי treats this like his other cases: the husband's silence backs up the witness. רבא says the case is different in kind. For a דבר שבערוה, the Torah requires two witnesses, so one witness is not enough even if the husband is quiet.
steps.whyThisMatters: This מחלוקת drives the rest of the section. Every proof that follows is an attempt to show that one witness is believed here, or to answer that attempt.

phrases.english: Abaye said: He is believed.
Rava said: He is not believed.
It is a matter of forbidden relations,
and no matter of forbidden relations is established by fewer than two witnesses.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: נֶאֱמָן. רָבָא אָמַר: אֵינוֹ נֶאֱמָן.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the two opposing answers to the question in Step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אביי: the single witness is believed. רבא: he is not, because a דבר שבערוה needs two witnesses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a מחלוקת. אביי believes the single witness; רבא requires two witnesses for ערוה.

steps.title: אביי's proof: the blind man and מר שמואל
steps.stepSummary: אביי tells a story. A messenger reported that a blind man's wife was unfaithful, and מר שמואל told the blind man to divorce her if he trusts the messenger.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: How do I know this? There was a blind man who used to review משניות before מר שמואל. One day he was late. מר שמואל sent a messenger after him, but they went by different roads and missed each other. When the messenger came back, he said that the blind man's wife had been unfaithful. The blind man asked מר שמואל, who said: If you trust him, go divorce her; if not, don't.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a real case to support his view that one witness is believed. Here the only witness to the wife's adultery is a single messenger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There was only one witness, yet מר שמואל said the husband could divorce his wife based on him. אביי will argue in the next step that this shows one witness is enough. The key question is what מר שמואל meant by 'if you trust him.'

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say it? (introduces a proof)
Send her out, meaning divorce her.

phrases.english: Abaye said: From where do I say it?
For there was a certain blind man

phrases.aramaic: דַּהֲוָה מְסַדַּר מַתְנְיָיתָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּמָר שְׁמוּאֵל.
phrases.english: who used to review mishnayot before Mar Shmuel.
One day he was late
and was not coming.
Mar Shmuel sent a messenger after him.
While the messenger went by one road,
the blind man came by another.
When the messenger came back, he said:
His wife committed adultery.
The blind man came before Mar Shmuel.
Mar Shmuel said to him: If he is trusted by you,
go divorce her,
and if not, do not divorce her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: אביי brings a story to support his position from Step 7.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's view that one witness is believed about a wife's adultery.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of the blind man and מר שמואל, where a single messenger reported the adultery.

steps.title: אביי reads 'if you trust him' as 'if he is a valid witness'
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains מר שמואל's words: 'if you trust him' means 'if you know he is not a thief,' that is, a kosher witness. So one valid witness is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: Doesn't it mean: if you trust that he is not a thief (and so is a valid witness)?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains how the story proves his point. He reads מר שמואל's words in a way that makes a single valid witness enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'trusted' only means 'not disqualified,' like a thief would be, then any honest single witness can be relied on. That would show one witness is believed in a matter of ערוה.

keyTerms.meaning: What, is it not...? (introduces a suggested reading)
A thief or robber. Such a person cannot serve as a witness.

phrases.english: What, is it not that it means:
If he is trusted by you
that he is not a thief?
phrases.notes: A thief can't be a witness. So this just means: if he's a normal, kosher witness, rely on him.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי לָאו אִי מְהֵימַן עֲלָךְ דְּלָאו גַּזְלָנָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the actual proof out of the story in Step 8.
steps.raayaObject: One valid witness is believed for a wife's adultery.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Reading מר שמואל's 'if you trust him' as 'if he is a kosher witness.'

steps.title: רבא: 'trust him like two witnesses'
steps.stepSummary: רבא reads מר שמואל differently: only if you trust this one man as much as two witnesses should you divorce her. So the story is no proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא says it means: If you trust him as much as two witnesses, go divorce her; if not, do not divorce her.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers אביי's proof by reading the same words in a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, 'trusted' means trusted so completely that it is as if two witnesses came. That is a personal matter for the husband and not normal court testimony. So the rule that ערוה needs two witnesses still stands.
steps.confusionAlert: Both אביי and רבא accept the same story. They argue only about what 'if you trust him' means: 'not a thief' (אביי) or 'like two witnesses' (רבא).

phrases.english: And Rava explains:
If he is trusted by you like two witnesses,
go divorce her,
and if not, do not divorce her.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָבָא: אִי מְהֵימַן לָךְ כְּבֵי תְרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי's reading in Step 9 by reinterpreting מר שמואל's words.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the blind man story only. רבא accepts the story itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'Trusted' does not mean merely 'not a thief.' It means trusted as much as two witnesses, so the story says nothing about one ordinary witness.

steps.title: אביי's second proof begins: the story of ינאי המלך
steps.stepSummary: אביי starts a new proof from a ברייתא. ינאי המלך returns from a great victory and holds a celebration with the חכמים, eating salty foods on golden tables.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי said: How do I know this? As a ברייתא teaches: King ינאי went to כוחלית in the desert and conquered sixty cities there. When he came back, he was very happy. He called all the חכמים of Israel and said to them: Our fathers ate salty foods when they were busy building the בית המקדש. We too will eat salty foods in their memory. They brought salty foods on golden tables and ate.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי opens a second proof by starting to quote a ברייתא. This part only sets up the story. The detail that proves his point comes in Step 13, and the proof itself is drawn out in Steps 17-18.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing about one witness has come up yet. The scene of the king's feast is the background needed for what happens next. The learner should hold on and wait for the story to continue.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא.
An incident, a story that really happened.

phrases.english: And Abaye said: From where do I say it?
As it is taught in a baraita:
There was an incident with King Yannai
who went to Kochalit in the desert
and conquered sixty cities there.
On his return, he was very happy.
He called all the Sages of Israel
and said to them:
Our fathers used to eat salty foods

phrases.aramaic: בִּזְמַן שֶׁהָיוּ עֲסוּקִים בְּבִנְיַן בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ,
phrases.english: when they were busy building the Temple.
We too will eat salty foods
in memory of our fathers.

phrases.aramaic: וְהֶעֱלוּ מְלוּחִים עַל שׁוּלְחָנוֹת שֶׁל זָהָב, וְאָכְלוּ.
phrases.english: They brought up salty foods on golden tables, and they ate.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר אַבָּיֵי: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבא deflected the first proof in Step 10, אביי opens a second proof from a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's view that one witness is believed about a matter like this.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about ינאי המלך. The proving detail appears later in the story.

steps.title: אלעזר בן פועירה accuses the פרושים and suggests a loyalty test
steps.stepSummary: אלעזר בן פועירה tells ינאי המלך that the פרושים secretly dislike him and suggests he test them by wearing the ציץ. The king does it.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a wicked scoffer there named אלעזר בן פועירה. He told the king: 'The פרושים are against you in their hearts.' The king asked: 'What should I do?' He answered: 'Make them stand for the ציץ on your forehead.' So the king did.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps telling the story that אביי started. This part sets up the conflict between the king and the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing is proven yet. The story is building toward the key event, a rumor that gets investigated. Standing for the ציץ was a way of forcing the חכמים to show respect to the king as כהן גדול.

keyTerms.meaning: The gold plate worn on the forehead of the כהן גדול

phrases.english: And there was one person there,
a scoffer, a man with an evil heart, and a scoundrel,
and his name was Elazar ben Po'ira.

phrases.aramaic: וַיֹּאמֶר אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן פּוֹעֵירָה לְיַנַּאי הַמֶּלֶךְ:
phrases.english: And Elazar ben Po'ira said to King Yannai:

phrases.aramaic: יַנַּאי הַמֶּלֶךְ, לִבָּם שֶׁל פְּרוּשִׁים עָלֶיךָ.
phrases.english: King Yannai, the hearts of the Pharisees are against you.
The king asked: And what shall I do?
Make them stand up for the frontplate between your eyes.
phrases.notes: The ציץ has ה׳'s name on it, so they would have to stand up. Their reaction would show their attitude toward the king.

phrases.english: He made them stand up for the frontplate between his eyes.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָיָה שָׁם אֶחָד, אִישׁ לֵץ לֵב רַע וּבְלִיַּעַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא that אביי introduced in step 11.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that one witness is believed even in matters of ערוה

steps.title: The rumor about ינאי's mother is investigated and not proven
steps.stepSummary: יהודה בן גדידיה tells the king to give up the priesthood because of a rumor that his mother was a captive. The rumor is checked, nothing is found, and the חכמים are driven away in anger.
steps.simpleTranslation: An elder named יהודה בן גדידיה said: 'King, being king is enough for you. Leave the priesthood to the children of אהרן.' This was because people said the king's mother had been taken captive in מודיעים. They looked into it and found nothing. The חכמים were sent away in anger.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the heart of the story for אביי's proof. A claim that would make the king a חלל is investigated and cannot be proven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman who was taken captive may not marry a כהן, so her son would be a חלל and unfit to serve as כהן גדול. The words 'it was investigated and not found' are the key line. The גמרא will soon look closely at this line to see what kind of testimony was needed.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter was investigated and not found

steps.whyThisMatters: אביי's whole proof depends on the phrase 'investigated and not found.' Notice it carefully.

phrases.english: There was a certain elder there
and his name was Yehuda ben Gedidya,

phrases.aramaic: וַיֹּאמֶר יְהוּדָה בֶּן גְּדִידְיָה לְיַנַּאי הַמֶּלֶךְ:
phrases.english: and Yehuda ben Gedidya said to King Yannai:

phrases.aramaic: יַנַּאי הַמֶּלֶךְ! רַב לְךָ כֶּתֶר מַלְכוּת,
phrases.english: King Yannai! The crown of kingship is enough for you,

phrases.aramaic: הַנַּח כֶּתֶר כְּהוּנָּה לְזַרְעוֹ שֶׁל אַהֲרֹן.
phrases.english: leave the crown of priesthood to the descendants of Aaron.
For people were saying: his mother was taken captive in Modi'in.
phrases.notes: A captive woman can't marry a כהן, so her son would be a חלל. That is the point behind the elder's words.

phrases.english: The matter was investigated, and it was not found.
And the Sages of Israel were driven away in anger.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיָה שָׁם זָקֵן אֶחָד וִיהוּדָה בֶּן גְּדִידְיָה שְׁמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story. This is the event אביי will use as evidence.
steps.raayaObject: Whether one witness can be trusted about a question of family status
steps.raayaSupportSource: The line 'וַיְבוּקַּשׁ הַדָּבָר וְלֹא נִמְצָא' in the ברייתא

steps.title: אלעזר בן פועירה urges the king to destroy the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: אלעזר בן פועירה says sending the חכמים away is too light a punishment for a king and tells him to crush them. When the king asks about the Torah, he says it is lying in a corner for anyone to learn.
steps.simpleTranslation: אלעזר said: 'That is how an ordinary person would react. You are a king and a כהן גדול. Is that all you do?' The king asked: 'What should I do?' He said: 'If you take my advice, crush them.' The king asked: 'And what will happen to the Torah?' He answered: 'It is rolled up and lying in a corner. Whoever wants to learn can come and learn.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues the story. The conflict now turns violent, and the king is told he does not need the חכמים for Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This part does not add to the legal proof. It moves the story toward its tragic ending. Notice his claim that the Torah can be learned without teachers. The next step criticizes exactly that idea.

phrases.aramaic: וַיֹּאמֶר אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן פּוֹעֵירָה לְיַנַּאי הַמֶּלֶךְ:
phrases.english: And Elazar ben Po'ira said to King Yannai:

phrases.aramaic: יַנַּאי הַמֶּלֶךְ, הֶדְיוֹט שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל כָּךְ הוּא דִּינוֹ,
phrases.english: King Yannai, this is how a common person in Israel would be treated,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַתָּה מֶלֶךְ וְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל כָּךְ הוּא דִּינָךְ?
phrases.english: and you, a king and High Priest, is this how you are treated?
The king asked: And what shall I do?
If you listen to my advice: crush them.
The king asked: And what will become of the Torah?
Look, it is rolled up and lying in a corner,
anyone who wants to learn can come and learn.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַיֹּאמֶר אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן פּוֹעֵירָה לְיַנַּאי הַמֶּלֶךְ: יַנַּאי הַמֶּלֶךְ, הֶדְיוֹט שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל כָּךְ הוּא דִּינוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story after the חכמים are driven away.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that one witness is believed

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: the king's answer showed heresy
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק interrupts the ברייתא. He says the king accepted this answer because heresy had entered him. He should have asked: what about the תורה שבעל פה?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Right then, heresy entered the king. He should have answered: 'Fine for the written Torah, but what about the Oral Torah?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא briefly steps out of the ברייתא to add a comment from an אמורא about the king's reaction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The written Torah can sit in a corner, but the תורה שבעל פה lives only through the חכמים who pass it on. Agreeing to kill them showed that the king did not value the Oral Torah. רב נחמן בר יצחק calls that מינות.
steps.confusionAlert: These are not the words of the ברייתא. They are an inserted comment from רב נחמן בר יצחק. The ברייתא picks up again in the next step.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
Immediately, heresy was thrown into him,
because he should have said:
That works for the Written Torah,
but what about the Oral Torah?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: מִיָּד נִזְרְקָה בּוֹ מִינוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side comment on the king's acceptance of אלעזר's argument in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Accepting that the Torah needs no חכמים ignores the תורה שבעל פה. That is a sign of heresy.

steps.title: The חכמים are killed until שמעון בן שטח restores the Torah
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends: the evil spread through אלעזר בן פועירה, all the חכמים were killed, and the world was empty of Torah until שמעון בן שטח brought it back.
steps.simpleTranslation: Right away, the evil flared up through אלעזר בן פועירה. All the חכמים of Israel were killed, and the world was desolate, until שמעון בן שטח came and restored the Torah to what it had been.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its story. The גמרא is setting up for אביי to explain how this story proves his point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the story complete, the legal question returns. What did 'investigated and not found' mean, and what would have happened if one witness had been found? אביי will build his proof on that.

keyTerms.meaning: Blazed up, broke out like fire

steps.whatToRemember: The whole story is brought for one line: 'וַיְבוּקַּשׁ הַדָּבָר וְלֹא נִמְצָא.' The legal argument about one witness, between אביי and רבא, continues from there.

phrases.aramaic: מִיָּד: וַתּוּצַץ הָרָעָה עַל יְדֵי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן פּוֹעֵירָה,
phrases.english: Immediately, the evil blazed up through Elazar ben Po'ira,
and all the Sages of Israel were killed,
and the world was desolate,
until Shimon ben Shatach came
and restored the Torah to its former glory.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיָּד: וַתּוּצַץ הָרָעָה עַל יְדֵי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן פּוֹעֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the ברייתא again after רב נחמן בר יצחק's comment and brings it to its end.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that one witness is believed
steps.raayaSupportSource: End of the ברייתא about ינאי המלך

steps.title: How exactly was the rumor found to be false?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the case looked like when the rumor was checked and found false. It rejects the idea that it was two witnesses against two.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was the case? If you say two witnesses said 'she was captured' and two said 'she was not captured,' why rely on one pair? You could just as easily rely on the other pair!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the words 'the rumor was checked and nothing was found' and asks what kind of testimony this was. It rules out a case of two witnesses against two, which sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When two pairs of witnesses contradict each other (תרי ותרי), neither pair beats the other. So you could not say the rumor was 'found to be false.' The case must have been something else.

keyTerms.meaning: What does the case look like?
What did you see? Why prefer this side over that one?

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
phrases.notes: He means: how did they check the rumor about ינאי's mother and find nothing (Step 13)?

phrases.english: If you say that two said: "She was captured"
and two said: "She was not captured"
what did you see that you rely on these,
rely on these!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָמֵי? אִילֵּימָא דְּבֵי תְרֵי אָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא's words about checking the rumor (Step 13) and looks at them in legal terms.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What kind of testimony let them call the captivity rumor false?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not two witnesses against two, since then neither side wins.

steps.title: It must be one witness against two, which shows one witness is believed
steps.stepSummary: The case must be one witness who said she was captured against two who said she was not. So he lost only because two contradicted him. Without them he would be believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it was one witness. The only reason he was not believed is that two people contradicted him. This shows that otherwise he would be believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question: there was one witness against two. From this it draws a proof that a single witness is believed when no one contradicts him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lone witness was rejected only because two witnesses said the opposite. So if nobody had argued with him, his testimony would have stood. That fits the view of אביי that an uncontested עד אחד is believed in a case like this.

keyTerms.meaning: But if it were not so

steps.confusionAlert: The proof does not come from the outcome (the witness lost). It comes from the reason he lost: only because two contradicted him.

phrases.english: Rather, it was with one witness,
phrases.notes: One witness said she was captured, and two said she was not.

phrases.aramaic: וְטַעְמָא דְּקָא מַכְחֲשִׁי לֵיהּ בֵּי תְרֵי,
phrases.english: and the reason is that two contradict him,
so if not for that, he would be believed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בְּעֵד אֶחָד, וְטַעְמָא דְּקָא מַכְחֲשִׁי לֵיהּ בֵּי תְרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 17's question and turns the answer into a proof.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's view that an uncontested single witness is believed
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ינאי story: the lone witness lost only because two contradicted him

steps.title: רבא: it could still be two against two, as עדי הזמה
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the case really was two against two. The second pair did not just disagree. They made the first pair into עדים זוממין, which knocks out their testimony completely.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא? Really it was two against two, like רב אחא בר רב מניומי said elsewhere: the second pair were witnesses of הזמה. Here too, they were witnesses of הזמה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on the proof. He shows the case can be two against two after all, so it proves nothing about one witness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 said two against two is a tie. But if the second pair says 'you were with us somewhere else at that time,' that is הזמה, and the first pair is thrown out entirely. Then the rumor really was found false, with no need for a single witness.

keyTerms.meaning: Witnesses who show the first witnesses were somewhere else, which cancels their testimony

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up הזמה with ordinary contradiction. Contradiction is a tie. הזמה wipes out the first pair.

phrases.english: And רבא?
phrases.notes: He means: how would רבא, who disagrees with אביי, answer this proof?

phrases.english: Actually, it was two against two,

phrases.aramaic: וְכִדְאָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר רַב מִנְיוֹמֵי:
phrases.english: and as Rav Acha bar Rav Minyumi said:
with witnesses of הזמה.
Here too, it was with witnesses of הזמה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָבָא: לְעוֹלָם תְּרֵי וּתְרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in Step 18 by bringing back the two-against-two case from Step 17.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the ינאי story
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumed two against two must be a tie, but הזמה lets the second pair win.

steps.title: Another answer: a maidservant was taken in her place
steps.stepSummary: A second way for רבא to explain the story, following רבי יצחק: a maidservant was put in place of ינאי's mother. So the second pair explained what the first pair saw.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say it follows רבי יצחק, who said: they brought in a maidservant in her place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives one more way to read the story as two against two without proving anything about one witness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both pairs can be telling the truth. The first pair saw someone being taken. The second pair shows it was a שפחה swapped in for her, so the mother herself was never captured. Either way, the story is no proof for אביי.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say... (introduces another answer)

steps.whatToRemember: The ינאי story cannot settle the argument. אביי reads it as one witness against two. רבא reads it as two against two, explained by הזמה or by רבי יצחק's swapped maidservant.

phrases.english: And if you want, say it is like רבי יצחק,
for רבי יצחק said:
They brought in a maidservant in her place.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא כִּדְרַבִּי יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, separate way to reject the proof from Step 18, alongside Step 19.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the ינאי story
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The two pairs need not clash at all. The second pair explains that a maidservant was taken instead.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The story gives no proof for אביי.

steps.title: רבא begins a new statement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces a new statement from רבא. His words come in the next part of the text.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move by telling us that רבא is about to speak. This line only names the speaker, and his words come right after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two explanations of the ינאי story (Steps 19-20) are now finished. 'אָמַר רָבָא' opens a fresh statement, so the learner should get ready for a new point. Do not try to read a ruling into this line by itself.

keyTerms.meaning: said / says. This word opens a statement by a named sage.
A major אמורא from בבל. Steps 19-20 already brought his explanations of the ינאי story.

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a third explanation of the ינאי story. It is just the opening of whatever רבא says next, so hold off on deciding what it means until you read his words.

phrases.english: Rava says:

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the two ways רבא explained the ינאי story (Steps 19-20), the גמרא now brings a new statement from רבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not stated yet. This line only introduces the speaker, and the content follows in the next text.
